I can't find the official DMTF doc which shows PATCH example with LocationIndicatorActive.

Here is the assembly example - 
https://www.dmtf.org/sites/default/files/standards/documents/DSP2046_2025.2.html
- 6.10.5 Example response.

However, DMTF Assembly schema contains LocationIndicatorActive which is ReadW-rite.
- section 6.10.3 Properties

```
      LocationIndicatorActive (v1.3+)	boolean	read-write
(null)	An indicator allowing an operator to physically locate this resource.

```
https://redfishforum.com/thread/437/patch-individual-items-array-objects seems to differ from this
The new patch follows as described in forum link

Can you mention the MemberId and how it used in patching ? 

                "MemberId": {
                    "description": "The unique identifier for the member within an array.",
                    "longDescription": "This property shall contain the unique identifier for this member within an array.  For services supporting Redfish v1.6 or higher, this value shall contain the zero-based array index.",
MemberId is no longer used for PATCH, as it is readonly field and patching method follows the explanation in https://redfishforum.com/thread/437/patch-individual-items-array-objects

What happens if MemberId is ordered like below? It matches the 6th and 3th assembly in the array (Redfish states it is zero-based)

```
curl -k -H "X-Auth-Token: $token" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -X PATCH -d '{"Assemblies":[{"MemberId" : "5", "LocationIndicatorActive":true},{"MemberId": "2", "LocationIndicatorActive":true}]}'
```

MemberId is the key to find the matching entry in Assembly.
Only assembly items in Patch input are going to be patched. Other entries are not going to be touched.
The Patch input is not needed to be sorted.

this doesn't look right, do we need to check the ec here? Could be a separate commit. But not everything should be a resourceNotFound

`assembly_utils::getChassisAssembly()` checks `ec` whether it is an `io_error` or `EBADR`, and returns `internalError()` for the other cases.
If this function is called, they are the cases of NotFound, and this warning is to show show which one of `io_error` or `EBADR`.

Would my response answer your question?
Acknowledged. I don't see why io_error vs EBADR matters but it doesn't hurt anything.
Again this doesn't look correct, everything is being mapped to resourceNotFound?  Maybe a separate commit to fix this ?

Similar to GET - https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/84000/comment/b94ab48f_1ba0b540/, the error conditions, other than `io_error` or EBADR, are already handled as `internalError` inside `getChassisAssembly`.
If the code reaches here, ec will be only one of `io_error` or EBADR, but both cases are resulted as NotFound.
